span.text: the AI Governance Officer
reconciles the central AI inventory in ServiceNow with the IT application register
within 15 business days after quarter-end
Each quarter
The signed reconciliation is retained in the AI governance SharePoint folder
Every system found outside the inventory is added within 10 business days with an owner, purpose and provisional risk class

reviews.automation_rationale: Comparing the inventory with the application register, contract list and GenAI tool list is a rules-based match that could be scripted or run in a reconciliation tool.
reviews.suggested_rewrite: Each quarter, within 15 business days after quarter-end, the AI Governance Officer reconciles the central AI inventory in ServiceNow with the IT application register, the procurement contract list (contracts tagged 'AI' or with AI features) and the list of enabled GenAI tools, investigating every mismatch. Every system found outside the inventory is added within 10 business days with an owner, purpose and provisional risk class. A [independent reviewer role] signs the reconciliation, which is retained in the AI governance SharePoint folder.

reviews.suggested_rewrite: Before an AI system is put into use or its intended purpose changes, the AI Governance Officer classifies it using the AI classification questionnaire: prohibited practice (EU AI Act Art. 5), high-risk under Annex III, transparency obligations, or minimal risk, plus the internal materiality rating (high / medium / low) per [rating criteria]. The Chief Risk Officer reviews and approves the classification against [approval criteria]; the approved questionnaire is stored in the AI inventory, and no system is enabled in production without it.

'Management' is a group, not a named role. Name the accountable role, e.g. Head of AI Governance or HR Learning Lead.

evidence_span.text: makes sure employees are trained on AI

findings.message: No frequency is stated in the description or the frequency column. Specify how often the control operates, e.g. annually plus on joining.
'As needed' is not a trigger. Define when training is assigned, e.g. on joining, on role change, or before getting AI tool access.

reviews.automation_rationale: A learning management system could assign training and report completion automatically, but deciding who needs what content and following up remain manual.
reviews.suggested_rewrite: The [role, e.g. Head of AI Governance] assigns AI-awareness training to all employees who use or oversee AI systems [timing, e.g. within 30 days of joining or a role change, and before access to AI tools is granted], and repeats it [frequency, e.g. annually]. The [role] reviews the completion report from [system, e.g. LMS] and follows up on any incomplete assignments within [timeframe]. The completion report and follow-up records are retained in [evidence location].

span.text: the data pipeline for the credit-limit scoring model runs automated checks
runs automated checks on the input file: completeness of mandatory fields, value ranges, duplicates and data age
Every business day by 08:00
Every business day
The check results are logged in the data-quality dashboard
If more than 1% of records fail, the run is stopped automatically

reviews.automation_rationale: The checks, threshold-based run stop and incident creation are already automated, leaving only human incident resolution.
reviews.suggested_rewrite: Every business day by 08:00, the data pipeline for the credit-limit scoring model automatically checks the input file for completeness of mandatory fields, value ranges, duplicates and data age (no record older than 3 days). If more than 1% of records fail, the run is stopped automatically and a ServiceNow incident is opened for the Data Steward, who resolves it before the model is rerun. Check results are logged in the data-quality dashboard and incidents are retained in ServiceNow.

span.text: the Data Science Lead documents

each retraining
The signed data sheet is stored in the model repository
selection-rate ratio of at least 0.8 for each group versus the most selected group

reviews.automation_rationale: The bias test and the 0.8 threshold gate can be scripted into the retraining pipeline, leaving human sign-off only on the data sheet and exceptions.
reviews.suggested_rewrite: Before each retraining of the CV-screening model, the Data Science Lead documents the data sources, sampling period and representativeness by gender, age band and nationality, and runs the bias test suite (selection-rate ratio of at least 0.8 for each group versus the most selected group). The HR Analytics Manager reviews and signs the data sheet. Retraining does not proceed while any group is below 0.8. The signed data sheet is stored in the model repository.

findings.message: Nature is "Automated", but the description describes a manual step ("reviewed").
The description does not say what evidence of the alert and its review is kept, or where.
The platform is clear for the calculation and alert, but the reviewer of the alert is not named. Add a role.
Calculation and alerting are concrete, but 'reviewed' does not say what the reviewer does or what happens after review.
The threshold is not quantified, for example a PSI value, and no criterion is given for investigating or closing an alert.
The alert trigger is defined, but there is no deadline for reviewing the alert after it is raised.

reviews.automation_rationale: Drift calculation and alerting are already automated; only the exception-based human review and follow-up remain manual.
reviews.suggested_rewrite: Every [week, per frequency column], the forecasting platform calculates the population stability index for the key input features of the demand-forecasting model and sends an alert when drift exceeds [threshold, e.g. PSI > 0.2]. The Supply Chain Analytics Lead reviews each alert within [timing, e.g. 5 business days], investigates the cause, and records the conclusion and any action taken in the drift alert log at [evidence location].
